definition.en: All the water a place holds: groundwater, soil water, snow and ice, lakes and rivers. The GRACE satellites weigh it from space by feeling tiny changes in Earth's pull. Each month is compared with the same month's 2004–2009 average, so the usual wet and dry seasons drop out, and the year's value is the mean of those monthly changes, as a layer of water in centimetres. Below zero means the place holds less water than it did then.

source.resolution: about 3° mascons on a 0.5° grid, averaged to 1°

en: Very coarse: each value is spread over a patch about 300 km across, so it cannot see one province or one well field.
It is a change against the 2004–2009 average, not an amount of water. Zero does not mean dry.
Between the two satellite missions there is a gap from mid-2017 to mid-2018, so 2017 and 2018 have no value. A year needs at least 6 months of data.

notes:
Threshold for stats.T: a GRACE year counts only with at least 6 monthly solutions. Add `grace_min_months = 6` to `earthbuddy/stats.py` T; tools/grids/grace.py reads `getattr(T, 'grace_min_months', 6)`, so drop the default after the merge.
Months per year (JPL labels): 2002 7, 2003 11, 2004-2010 12, 2011 10, 2012 10, 2013-2016 9, 2017 5, 2018 5, 2019-2024 12. So 2017 and 2018 are NaN; 2001 is NaN (record starts Apr 2002). first_year 2002.
2002 has only Apr-Dec minus Jun/Jul, so its yearly mean leans to the wet season in the tropics (Cambodia 2002 = +27.4 cm vs about 0 in 2004-2009). Partial years in 2011-2016 are less skewed (missing months are spread out).
Month labels come from the file's months_missing attribute (record months minus missing, in order); time midpoints would put two solutions in Jan 2012 and Apr 2015, which JPL labels Dec 2011 and May 2015.
Value = lwe_thickness (cm) x scale_factor, land_mask == 1 only (ocean NaN). The CRI file DOES include `scale_factor` (CLM-based gain factors 'to be used with mascon solution that has the CRI filter applied'). They are blank over the Greenland/Antarctic ice sheets and reach 22x on Arctic ice caps (Ellesmere would read -65 m), because they are built for land hydrology, not glaciers. So they are applied between 60S and 60N only; poleward the value is unscaled. Ice-sheet cells still reach metres (Greenland coast -20 m in 2024), which is real ice loss.
Baseline: the file's anomaly is relative to 2004.000-2009.999 (time_mean_removed). The yearly 1° value is the mean of the 0.5° pixel centres in the cell; it does not make the 3° mascon any finer.
Source kind 'satellite' (gravimetry). Agency NASA: GRACE is NASA/DLR and GRACE-FO NASA/GFZ, but the mascon product is made and archived by NASA JPL.
Download: one 46,365,171-byte netCDF from archive.podaac.earthdata.nasa.gov (via netrc), the file covers 2002-04 to 2026-09. The script finds the newest granule by CMR and re-downloads only if the file name changed.
